response.justification: The candidate is a seasoned generalist engineer (14+ years) with strong systems thinking, low-latency/event-driven experience (DLang microservices at Sociomantic handling millions of req/s), and excellent testing, mentoring, and documentation credentials. However, the role is fundamentally a C++ engineering position in industrial automation, and the resume shows only ~6 months of professional C++/C work (National Instruments, 2014-2015) plus a university thesis — C++ is not even listed in the skills section. There is no evidence of MQTT, message brokers in an industrial context, IEC 62443/SDL secure development practices, OPC UA/Modbus/IEC 61850 protocols, Azure, or IoT/industrial automation domain exposure. The gap between the recent decade of TypeScript/Node/web work and the required hands-on modern C++ and industrial cybersecurity expertise is too large for a mid-senior hands-on role expected to mentor others on C++ and security standards.
strengths: Deep experience with high-throughput, low-latency, event-driven distributed systems
Strong engineering craft: TDD, CI/CD, testing tooling, mentoring, public workshops and talks
Broad polyglot background across embedded, desktop, backend and cloud/Kubernetes deployments
concerns: Minimal recent C++/STL experience — roughly 6 months professionally, over a decade ago
No IEC 62443, SDL, or industrial cybersecurity exposure evident
No industrial automation, MQTT, OPC UA/Modbus, or Azure background

key_factors.factor: Industrial cybersecurity / IEC 62443 and SDL gap
